ツレ猫 マルルとハチ [Tsureneko - Maruru to Hachi] #2

Maruru și Hachi Vol. 2: Pisicile hoinare

Yuri Sonoda, Malina Cosan (Translator)

4.52
665 ratings66 reviews
Rate this book
Maruru este o pisică de casă care, printr-o întâmplare nefericită, ajunge să trăiască pe stradă. Hachi, un motan cu privire tăioasă, e șeful pisicilor de pe teritoriul unde se refugiază Maruru.


Când bătrânica nu mai vine în parc să le hrănească, viața pisicilor devine și mai grea, iar situația se înrăutățește când Hachi e grav rănit... Pentru a supraviețui, cei doi motani trebuie să ia o decizie crucială!


Povestea a două pisici fără stăpân care înfruntă împreună provocările unei lumi necruțătoare.

Trigger warning that contains a small spoiler: There is a scene where it is implied that a cat passes away, from page 29-32. Please be aware if you are sensitive to the topic.
"I was only able to survive as a stray because you were with me, Hachi. So whatever happens now... I'll stick with you."

Some of my worries about the possibility of this series being too sad and real for me have been assuaged in this volume now that Maruru and Hachi are turning over a new leaf in a new location!

This volume focused a lot less on Maruru and Hachi's dynamic and more now on the lives of the cat shelter folks that live in their area. I hope we're building up to the two of them living happy and safe lives together from now on! I also cried a lot (of happiness and also just understanding) when Yasuo shed tears over finally getting to bring Hachi in. It is so painful to care a lot about animals like that, especially when anything can happen to strays who aren't being looked after, but I so completely understood his emotions in that moment.

This series already makes me so emotional! I can only give my heartfelt thanks and love to all the people out there who dedicate their lives to rescuing and looking after cats. I feel like this book is truly a love letter to them, and they deserve it. Cats are our precious friends and we must treat them well!! ;-;

Artemissia G
1,856 reviews41 followers
June 11, 2023
Le premier tome avait été une belle surprise avec ce récit sur des chats de rues que j’ai trouvé bien traité et avec beaucoup de profondeur. La suite est dans la même lignée. Nous retrouvons nos deux chamarades, Hachi le taciturne et sombre et Maruru, le chat un peu tête en l’air et rêveur.
Depuis que la vieille dame qui les nourrissait s’en est allée, nos chats ont bien du mal à se remplir le ventre chaque jour. Cela entraine des situations terribles et des décisions parfois difficiles vont devoir être prises. Mais, quoi qu’il se passe, Maruru ne laissera jamais tomber Hachi. J’aime ce lien qui s’est créé entre eux. C’est très beau.

On va en découvrir plus du côté du jeune homme qui capture les chats et qui les ramène à son association. D’ailleurs, c’est l’occasion, pour nous lecteur. rice. s d’en apprendre plus sur ces personnes qui s’occupent au quotidien des chats errants. J’ai beaucoup aimé cet aspect du manga qui ne se focalise pas que sur nos ami. e. s à quatre pattes.
Pour ce qui est des dessins, j’aime toujours autant même si j’ai une préférence pour les animaux aux humains.

Hachi et Maruru – Chats des rues est un manga qui ne s’arrête pas simplement sur l’aspect mignon des chats. Au contraire, il prend le temps de nous dépeindre l’histoire de ceux qui survivent dans la rue avec leur lot de joie, de tristesse et d’amusement. Dans l’ensemble, c’est un titre qui me rappelle un vieux dessin animé que je regardais enfant, Les entrechats. Comme quoi, le sujet ne nous intéresse pas que d’aujourd’hui.

Une suite plaisante et un seinen que je vais continuer avec plaisir.

May 10, 2025
This is cute, BUT.

...

I don't know. I know there are realistically SO MANY stray cats but only a handful of characters, so it feels ridiculously contrived when , for the sake of a cute moment. This is even when Yasuo has just gotten back from helping with a hoarding issue!

Also, how do the humans know the cats' names? How are they absolutely certain Hachi is the same Hachi as the Hachi named by... whoever named him that? Maruru, also—that's probably his name on the microchip, but that's also generally what EVERYBODY calls him. Slight plothole, here!

The rest of the book is okay, going into the somewhat difficult problem of being a stray in an environment that's increasingly hostile toward strays: the few people willing to feed the cats no longer can, some (unwittingly?) poison the cats, and others—like Maruru's former owners just giving up and getting a new cat, basically condemning Maruru to his fate by locking him out once he got out—just plain neglecting them.

It's a balance, though, I know. Some cats are good—they keep the vermin population down! However, they also keep the overall "critter" population down, too, killing a very large number of birds (whether you argue they're also "vermin"). So LOTS of cats are bad, even if you happen to love cats (like me) but can't remotely save all of them (also like me... and most people).

I sort of don't see this story going much farther than book 3 (despite there being a listing for book 5?), since... how much more can they do? Sure, there are plenty of books about rescued cats, but this one seemed to hit a major shift just in book 2, with the Stray For Life stray voluntarily getting himself trapped when he was close to death. Kind of a tough act to follow!

Not that I don't want to see what happens next! I just have a tough time imagining what's next (which is why I'll have to see, haha).

December 4, 2024
Après avoir lu le premier tome, je me suis aussitôt jetée sur la suite. Ce manga est tout simplement incroyable. Comme je l’ai déjà dit pour le premier tome, je ne m’attendais absolument pas à pleurer autant pendant ma lecture. Je m’attendais à quelque chose de drôle et de léger alors que finalement c’est une histoire pleine d’émotions et tellement touchante. Ce second tome était aussi émouvant que le premier. Par contre, j’aime beaucoup le chemin que l’histoire prend, je suis très curieuse de lire la suite.

Dans ce second tome, Maruru, devenu chat errant malgré lui, vit maintenant dans la rue avec Hachi, un savant et courageux boss de territoire. Mais depuis que la grand-mère qui les nourrissait chaque jour dans le parc n’y vient plus, ils peinent tous les deux à trouver de quoi manger… Et la situation se corse encore quand Hachi revient blessé d’une énième bataille de chats errants ! L’importante décision que ce dernier prendra alors va complètement changer leur quotidien, les menant à connaître un tout autre environnement et style de vie.

Bon, bien entendu j’ai encore passé beaucoup de temps à me moucher pendant ma lecture. On a encore des moments extrêmement touchants, qui m’ont fait beaucoup de peine. Mais comme je viens de le dire un peu plus haut, j’adore le chemin que prend l’histoire, ça nous promet une suite tellement intéressante. Maruru a beau avoir appris des tas de choses aux côtés de Hachi, il ne se fera jamais vraiment à vivre dans l’errance. Et ça tombe bien puisque les choses vont finir par changer. J’ai beaucoup aimé découvrir ces humains qui terrorisent tant nos petits minous. L’histoire de la créatrice du refuge m’a arraché des larmes, bah oui que voulez vous.. j’ai adoré découvrir cette part de l’histoire et voir tout ce qu’elle fait pour les chats errants avec, parfois, si peu de moyens j’ai trouvé ça extraordinaire. J’ai trop hâte de lire la suite, ça tombe bien je l’ai avec moi haha

Un second tome dans la lignée du premier, toujours aussi émouvant. J’aime les petites infos utiles que l’on nous glisse par ci par là. Et on ne le dira jamais assez mais ne prenez pas d’animaux si vous n’êtes pas capable de vous en occuper, ce ne sont pas des jouets, ce sont des êtres vivants. Adopter un animal c’est s’engager sur le long terme. N’abandonnez pas vos animaux c’est tellement cruel..

Maruru and Hachi continue to be cute, endearing, and fun. But also, this second volume has some really emotional moments; or so it felt for me as a cat owner, and especially as former owner of an elder cat that passed away, as well as a volunteer in an animal shelter (plus having lickables loving cats, lol).

I really liked how this series takes a realistic approach to the cats lives, that now includes some informative tips about things like TNR programs, and other very useful facts.

These cats are the absolute best, and I really want to know what is going to happen to them now that they are going through training and living the shelter life; and even more so, what will happen after that.

Content Warning: the manga is listed as ages 10+ but due to intense situations facing stray cats that are dealt with realistically (sensitive subjects like TNR are described as well), I would only recommend it for middle school ages 12 & up.

The bromance between Maruru and Hachi continues as the street cats tough it out to survive which faces Hachi to make a life-changing decision that does make this one a little happier in tone (still keep your box of tissue handy if you're an animal lover, especially a herder of cats such as myself).
